My Story

More Than a Student.
A Builder.

Where curiosity refused to stay quiet

Growing up in Kenya, Laurette Achieng' watched the world of science and technology feel like it belonged to someone else — someone else's country, someone else's gender, someone else's dream. But curiosity has a way of overriding every barrier placed in front of it. From her earliest years, questions about the human body, disease, data, and the mechanics of life itself refused to go quiet.

The scientist in the making

Laurette holds a BSc in Biomedical Science and Technology from Egerton University, graduating with Second Class Honours (Upper Division) in November 2026 — a degree she pursued with the same relentless energy she brings to everything else. Her training spans microbiology, bioinformatics, and genomics, and she has spent real hours in real laboratories, working through the kind of detail that turns curiosity into competence.

Her most formative research experience came during her industrial attachment at KEMRI-CGHR in Kisumu — Kenya's premier public health research institute — where she rotated through microbiology, entomology, malaria, and neglected tropical disease labs, including field activities such as mosquito identification, marking, and recapture. She also completed a genomics and bioinformatics internship at the GENOMAC Institute, gaining hands-on experience in sequence retrieval, codon and ORF identification, and primer design. Science, for Laurette, is not theoretical. It is lived.

From a gap she saw to a movement she built

While still a student, Laurette looked around and saw the girls in her community disengaging from science and technology — not from lack of ability, but from lack of access, mentorship, and mirrors. She did not wait for someone else to solve it. She founded STEMHER Africa: a grassroots initiative delivering STEM education, mentorship, leadership development, and confidence-building programmes directly to girls across Kenya. STEMHER Africa is not a side project. It is a statement of belief that African girls belong at the frontiers of science and innovation — and the data, the discipline, and the drive to make that real.

Building alongside the work

Beyond STEMHER Africa, Laurette serves as a STEM Trainer and Programme Representative at STEM Impact Centre Kenya, where she manages school outreach, facilitates science and technology programmes, and represents the organisation across Nakuru County and beyond. She has presented STEMHER Africa's research at the U.S. Embassy's American Spaces in Nakuru, facilitated and judged the World Robot Olympiad 2026 at Nova Pioneer, and participated in the Red White & Build: US-Kenya AI & Tech Hackathon. Her work is not theoretical. It leaves a mark.

What she is building toward

Laurette's vision is clear: an Africa where scientific excellence and equitable access to technology are inseparable — where the next generation of biomedical researchers, data scientists, health innovators, and science communicators emerge from every corner of the continent. She is building toward that future with every workshop delivered, every girl mentored, and every research question she refuses to stop asking.

Science & Research

Grounded in rigorous biomedical science and technology training — from wet lab techniques at KEMRI-CGHR in Kisumu to genomics work at GENOMAC Institute — Laurette approaches research with the belief that African scientists must be central to the conversations shaping African health.

Impact Focus: Evidence-Based Health Solutions
02

Leadership & Social Impact

As Founder and Executive Director of STEMHER Africa and STEM Trainer and Programme Representative at STEM Impact Centre Kenya, Laurette translates vision into real programmes — building communities, managing partnerships, and leading with the consistency that earns trust from institutions and students alike.

Impact Focus: Girls' Empowerment & Equity
03

STEM Education & Innovation

Laurette designs and delivers STEM and technology experiences that meet students exactly where they are — hands-on, culturally grounded, and built for lasting impact. From robotics at American Spaces Nakuru to science bootcamps at Moi Girls Eldoret and Sing'ore Girls, she is building toward an EdTech vision that can scale quality science and technology education to communities that need it most.

Impact Focus: Quality & Access in Science & Technology
04

Data, Technology & Innovation

From using R and Python for antimicrobial resistance analysis to participating in the U.S. Embassy's AI & Tech Hackathon Kenya, Laurette bridges biomedical science with data analytics and emerging technology. She sees computational tools not as add-ons, but as essential for the kind of research and education work that scales.

Impact Focus: Data-Driven Science & EdTech

Social Impact · Founding

STEMHER Africa

Founder & Executive Director · Since September 2025

ProblemGirls in Kenya disengage from science and technology as early as Grade 4 — not from lack of ability, but from lack of access, mentors, and role models. Only 36.59% of Kenya's STEM university placements go to girls.
ActionFounded STEMHER Africa to deliver early-start bootcamps, mentorship, leadership development, and confidence-building programmes — reaching girls at Moi Girls Eldoret, Sing'ore Girls, and American Spaces Nakuru.
RoleFounder, curriculum designer, lead facilitator, public advocate, and partnership manager.
LessonAccess alone does not create inclusion. A girl can sit in a science classroom and still feel like a visitor. Real inclusion is structural — and it starts early.
🌟  1,000+ students reached · Moi Girls Eldoret, Sing'ore Girls & more · SDGs 4, 5 & 10

Research

Final Year
Research Project.

Applying biomedical science and data analytics to a question that matters for East Africa's public health.

Undergraduate Research · Egerton University · 2025–2026

Comparative Analysis of Antimicrobial Resistance in Staphylococcus aureus from East African Isolates

ScopeMulti-country comparative study using isolates and data from Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania
Focus GenesResistance-associated genes including mecA, vanA/vanB, and blaZ
MethodsMolecular analysis, resistance gene profiling, and statistical analysis and visualization in R
ConnectionLinks directly to KEMRI-CGHR field experience and GENOMAC Institute bioinformatics training

Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is one of the most critical public health challenges facing East Africa — and Staphylococcus aureus sits at the centre of it. This project examined resistance patterns across three East African countries, identifying shared and distinct resistance gene profiles to better understand how AMR spreads across borders and what that means for regional health policy.

The analysis drew on Laurette's combined training in wet lab techniques, bioinformatics, and data analytics — using R for statistical analysis and visualization to translate raw molecular data into findings with real public health relevance.

Antimicrobial Resistance Molecular Microbiology Bioinformatics R · Statistical Analysis East Africa · Public Health S. aureus mecA · vanA/vanB · blaZ
